name: Pan-Latinism
summary: Pan-Latinism holds that the peoples of Romance-language descent in Europe and the Americas form one civilization (the Latin race, understood as linguistic and cultural) and should draw closer politically, culturally and economically, partly as a counterweight to Germanic, Slavic and Anglo-Saxon powers. It has two main strands: an imperial one that cast France as leader of the Latin world, and a democratic, confederal one that sought a federation of free Latin peoples without empire. Most of its concrete achievements were cultural societies and festivals, the Latin Monetary Union of 1865 and the later Latin Union (1954-2012).
scope: The profile represents the confederal, republican mainstream of the idea: Bilbao's 1856 Iniciativa de la America, Ricard's 1878 Federation of Latin Peoples, Charles-Brun's Latin confederation, and the cultural-institutional Latin Union. The imperial strand (Chevalier, Napoleon III, Stendhal, Hanotaux) and the Fascist-era Latin Axis idea are treated as minority strands that would answer imperial and expansion items differently. Most economic, social and modern issues were never addressed and are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Michel Chevalier
keyFigures.role: French Saint-Simonian who contrasted a Latin race with the Anglo-Saxons and popularised the idea in France.

keyFigures.name: Francisco Bilbao
keyFigures.role: Chilean writer whose 1856 Paris address urged a federal union of the Latin American republics.

keyFigures.name: Napoleon III
keyFigures.role: French emperor who made Latin leadership part of French policy, including the Mexican intervention.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Never a pan-Latin theme; inferred from the later Latin Union states, which are mostly welfare states with public health systems.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred from the broadly social-democratic politics of the Latin European and Latin American states it addressed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Not a pan-Latin theme; the Latin Monetary Union shows a preference for state-managed monetary coordination, so strong market faith is not inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents never took a line on it; Latin republican heirs range from state-ownership to liberal views.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's social, communal ideal and his criticism of oligarchic constitutions; the movement itself set no tax policy.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the republican and communal tone of Bilbao and Ricard; unions are not discussed in the sources.

property-fundamental.rationale: Sources are silent; Bilbao prefers the social over the individual, but liberal Latinists were not property critics.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No pan-Latin source addresses corporate regulation; no basis for a lean either way.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's preference for justice and the social over the individual; welfare was not at issue.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not discussed by Latinists; the movement was cultural and geopolitical, not about firm ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anachronistic issue for a 19th-century movement; its republican strands would be wary, its imperial strand indifferent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be inferred from Latin unity ideas.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; the Latin Union's human-rights commitment points one way, free-expression republicanism the other.

strong-leader.rationale: Bilbao rejects despotic centralization and the confederal strand rejects empire, though the Napoleon III strand leaned Caesarist.

state-harmful.rationale: Bilbao and Ricard want institutions (a federal congress, tribunal, confederation), so a Latinist rejects the claim that the state is unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by any Latinist source; the movement had no gun policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: Imperial strand favored French power, confederal strand did not; no consistent view.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the generally conventional, Catholic-cultured Latin milieu; not discussed.

decide-locally.rationale: The Félibrige and Charles-Brun strand paired Latin unity with regional autonomy, and Bilbao called for decentralization.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's humanitarian republicanism and the Latin Union's human-rights condition; prisons are not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Not discussed; Catholic-Latin traditionalists and secular republican Latinists would split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; modern Latin Union members are split, from legalizing states to restrictive ones.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic and split between secular-republican and Catholic Latinists.

more-religion-public.rationale: Bilbao demanded strict Church-State separation and Ricard opposed Catholic Caesarism, though Latin identity is often cast as Catholic.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Bilbao denounced the treatment of Indigenous peoples and slavery in the US, which implies support for redress; modern policy is inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources say nothing and Latin states differ.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Latin Union aimed to preserve the shared cultural heritage of Latin peoples, and Latinist festivals celebrated Latin literature and tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Imperial Latinists favored order, Bilbao and republican federalists favored radical republican creation; no common line.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Latin American and Mediterranean states have been emigration countries and Latinist circles took no stand.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Latinists built their own international bodies (the Latin Union, the monetary union), so they favor transnational institutions, though this is inferred for the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Bilbao backed abolishing internal customs and a federal trade pact among the republics, but the movement also sought a counterweight to Anglo-Saxon power.

nation-first.rationale: Pan-Latinism asks nations to unite across borders and put shared Latin interests ahead of separate national ones.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The imperial strand justified intervention (Mexico), while Bilbao and the confederal strand condemned conquest; split.

open-borders.rationale: Bilbao proposed universal citizenship across the American republics, but nothing suggests a global open-borders view.

limit-growth.rationale: Bilbao warned against Europe's and the US's wealth-pursuit and favored moral ends over wealth, but no environmental position is documented.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a Latinist topic; inferred from the Latin Union's modern member states, whose governments largely accept climate action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; 19th-century Saint-Simonian Latinists like Chevalier were technocratic progressives, but later strands were not.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic with no source basis; France is nuclear-friendly while others are not.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bilbao was a revolutionary republican exile but the Napoleon III and Latin Union strands were establishment; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Bilbao grounded his plan in popular sovereignty and universal suffrage; Saint-Simonian technocracy is a minority thread.

central-planning.rationale: Not addressed; Chevalier's Saint-Simonian planning ideas were not a movement position.

socialized-markets.rationale: No source speaks to this; Bilbao's communal ideal makes it neither rejected nor endorsed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a pan-Latin theme and not discussed in any source.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's attack on oligarchic power and the republican hostility to inherited privilege.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; the republican and Catholic social strands of Latin politics point opposite ways.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Latin unity projects mixed customs-union aims with Latin American protectionism; no settled line.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Saint-Simonian roots favored public works and planning, but the movement took no common economic line.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Bilbao's republic is communal and broad-based, but Latinists left property structure open and liberal and social strands diverge.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Latin Monetary Union was built to standardize money, so abolishing it is far from the movement; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The monetary union presupposes managed state currencies; inferred, not documented.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; only some fascist-era Latin Axis ideas were corporatist, and they are not the core.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bilbao's popular sovereignty and the republican confederal strand are opposed to single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Ricard's Latin federalism was republican and opposed to Caesarian monarchy, and Bilbao saw monarchy as Europe's flaw; the Napoleonic empire strand differs.

democracy-best.rationale: Bilbao grounds the union in popular sovereignty and universal suffrage, and Charles-Brun called for a democratic Latin confederation.

direct-votes.rationale: Bilbao favored popular self-representation but the sources do not discuss referendums as a mechanism.

workers-councils.rationale: Not in the sources; Bilbao's call for a congress of states points to representative bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Regional autonomy was valued, but unity was the aim, so secession is not endorsed by sources.

natural-rulers.rationale: Bilbao rejected aristocracy and hereditary rule in favor of sovereign citizens.

political-violence-never.rationale: Bilbao accepted defense and revolution; Latin Union members are peaceful; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Bilbao proposed arbitration before war; inferred opposition, not discussed directly.

separate-church-state.rationale: Bilbao calls strict Church-State separation a principle of his proposed congress; Ricard opposed clerical Caesarism; some Catholic Latinists dissent.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Bilbao rejects theocratic pacification and the Latin Union is a secular body.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Bilbao proposed an international tribunal and federal institutions; privatization is foreign to the sources.

military-superiority.rationale: Imperial Latinists wanted French or Latin dominance; the confederal strand rejected empire.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Latin race was defined by language and geography, not biological descent, and Bilbao saw a mixed Latin, Indigenous and Saxon America.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bilbao and the republican Latinists framed history around liberty and union, not class; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Bilbao preferred justice to power but equality of outcome was not a pan-Latin theme.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Bilbao included Indigenous people in the Latin American nation and decried their extermination, yet proposed to civilize those he called barbarians.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Imperial Latinists defended Latin colonization of Africa and the Americas; anti-imperial strands might favor reparations; split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Latinism is defined by union among nations of a shared Latin civilization and culture, and the Latin Union membership rule was Latin-derived language and culture.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Bilbao criticized egoism and individualism and prized the communal over the individual.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Bilbao valued the social over the individual but also insisted on individual rights and integrity.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Bilbao's spiritual outlook might support it, but the sources never mention nature, so adherents are not shown to lean either way.

limit-population.rationale: Bilbao's plan included colonization and filling the continent with citizens, so population limits sit poorly with it; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Bilbao criticized Europe's division of labor but Latinists were not anti-industrial; inferred mild disagreement.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Bilbao feared the machine-like fragmentation of the person; no movement support documented.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; Saint-Simonian progressive and humanist-spiritual strands would split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Bilbao's insistence on sovereign citizens.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; no principle of the movement bears on it either way.

restore-past-order.rationale: Bilbao spoke of a new moral creation beyond the old world; the movement looked forward to union, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Bilbao's moral-political project, with ideals like union and liberty at its centre, suggests principle over pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Latinism worked through festivals, diplomacy, treaties and congresses rather than direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bilbao insisted on voluntary union without conquest and said peace is the unity of liberty, so means must reflect the free union sought.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Latinism is a civilizational project of republics, education and trade, and entirely foreign to this view.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Bilbao criticizes the division of labor as fragmenting the person, but proposes no abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Bilbao calls for justice but as republican rights and education, not a need-based communist distribution; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Bilbao's moral ordering of economy to social ends leans toward it, but no source states it and liberal Latinists differ.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred from the movement's lack of Marxist content; its monetary projects were commercial.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bilbao and Charles-Brun's democratic confederalism exclude class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Nothing in Latinism suggests collectivized agriculture; Bilbao's emphasis on individual integrity points against compulsion.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The movement framed war as rivalry between civilizations (Latin, Germanic, Slavic, Anglo-Saxon), not as a product of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Bilbao proposed a federal congress and shared institutions that imply common finance; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Bilbao's liberal republicanism and defence of freedom of thought are consistent with limiting the state to preventing harm; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Bilbao valued the communal, social character of Latin America over the individual, and Latinism centers peoples.

conscription.rationale: Bilbao envisioned a continental army under conditions; conscription itself is not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Bilbao grounds the union in popular sovereignty and universal suffrage; voting is central.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's moral and social view of the republic.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bilbao calls for justice, education and universal citizenship as conditions of freedom; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Latinism was driven by writers, philologists and academics, who would not see themselves as an unaccountable power; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Latin race was treated by scholars as a linguistic and geographic category, not a genetic one, and Bilbao spoke of mixed Latin, Indigenous and Saxon elements.

organic-representation.rationale: Bilbao favored equal state representation in a congress, but corporate representation is not discussed.

total-state.rationale: Bilbao and the confederal strand reject despotic centralization.

national-rebirth.rationale: Bilbao spoke of a new moral creation in America, but decadence-rebirth rhetoric is not core to the movement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The imperial strand (Stendhal, Hanotaux) sought Latin expansion, while Bilbao and Charles-Brun rejected conquest; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Foreign to the republican Latinists; Bilbao rejects hierarchical obedience as a Spanish colonial legacy.

bound-labor.rationale: Bilbao condemns slavery and servitude as an inheritance to overcome.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Anachronistic; Latinism's rationalist, humanist heritage points against it.

universal-morality.rationale: Bilbao spoke of love of humankind and a moral basis for union; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Bilbao's moral unity of the continent leans to it, while confederal pluralism leans against.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No Latinist position; the movement's states include both supporters and critics of Zionism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; Latinism concerns Latin peoples' union, not diaspora return.

revive-national-language.rationale: Latin Union promoted Latin languages and Romanian, Occitan and Catalan revivalists took part, but state revival is not stated.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's insistence on self-representation and sovereign citizens as opposed to servile roles.

school-vouchers.rationale: Bilbao and Ricard wanted public universal education and a Pan-American university; vouchers contradict this on inference.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The monetary union failed partly through paper money for deficits, but the movement took no stand.

economic-freedom.rationale: No source ties political liberty to economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Bilbao grounded order in constitutions, a congress and a tribunal, not in the moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Romanian, Occitan and Catalan revivalists used Latinity to claim recognition, and Bilbao supported republican self-government.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; the imperial strand backed force while the confederal strand did not.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Bilbao was anticlerical, yet Latin identity is often Catholic; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Bilbao proposed universal citizenship among the republics, but welfare is not discussed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Anachronistic; Latin welfare traditions (Christian-democratic and social-democratic) differ.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's unity-of-liberty and the movement's nonclass framing.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage preservation was a stated aim of the Latin Union and of the Latinist festivals.

dominated-front.rationale: Pan-Latinism arose as a counterweight to Germany, Britain and the United States, and Bilbao urged union against US and European domination.

workers-nation.rationale: Latinism united peoples by civilization across borders, not workers along national lines; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The movement was not about gender; Catholic and republican Latinists differ.

ban-interest.rationale: The Latin Monetary Union itself operated within ordinary banking and coinage; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Bilbao held that Latin America is a mixed society and criticized US treatment of slavery and Indigenous peoples.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Non-Marxist; Bilbao saw oligarchic constitutions as capturing the state but proposed republican reform.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; Latin states split between producers (Mexico, Venezuela) and importers.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Bilbao saw Latin America as open to mixed peoples, while French strands assimilated; no clear view.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the movement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Bilbao proposed equal state representation and counted votes by individuals, but legislative systems are not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Napoleon III presented France as leader of the Latin peoples and spread Latin civilization; confederal strands rejected a mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement had no gender doctrine and Latin republicans and Catholics diverge.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Bilbao attacked oligarchic constitutions, but this was not a general theme.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Foreign to Bilbao's humanism and the Latin Union's human-rights condition; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Latin Union required human-rights and democratic principles for membership, which implies accountability for abuses; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Bilbao's federal congress with education, a university and trade agenda implies an active public role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Bilbao celebrated a mixed Latin, Indigenous and Saxon America.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Bilbao affirmed universal citizenship and room in the heart for all humanity, and the Latin Union asks for human-rights commitment.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist debate irrelevant to Latinism, which took no stance on it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Bilbao condemned Spanish conquest yet counted Latin America as the heir; split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Bilbao proposed one common code across the republics and French republicanism favors uniform civil law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Bilbao defended freedom of thought and rejected theocratic pacification.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No Latin relevance; Latin cuisines and cultures use beef.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Bilbao and the republican strand opposed clerical control of education; Catholic Latinists differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Foreign to the republican confederal tradition and its rejection of despotic centralization.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bilbao grounds legitimacy in popular sovereignty and requires each state's approval of congress decisions.

trade-surplus.rationale: The movement had no mercantilist doctrine; the monetary union aimed at easier trade.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts Bilbao's inclusive humanism and the rejection of conquest.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Bilbao rejects conquest but accepts defense and armed forces; the imperial strand did not.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Bilbao argued for peace and cooperation among republics rather than struggle; the imperial strand differs.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Bilbao defended freedom of thought and republican liberty; party bans are inferred as unwelcome.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Bilbao's condemnation of despotism and foreign domination reads as non-domination, though he does not use the term.

separated-powers.rationale: Bilbao's federal congress, equal state representation and arbitration tribunal imply divided authority.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bilbao's popular, democratic basis and confederal Latinism rule out a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Bilbao preferred justice to power and the social to the individual; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Anachronistic national housing policy that the movement never touched.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's republican liberty and social orientation.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Bilbao blamed oligarchic institutions and colonial legacy, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Bilbao saw a mixed Latin America as a strength with room for all.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Bilbao backs universal suffrage and representation by election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Bilbao grounds the union on rights and liberty.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not a Latinist subject; Latin economies include both interventionist and liberal traditions.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bilbao defended freedom of thought and republican liberty, which excludes party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; Bilbao proposed federal command over joint forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Bilbao proposed universal citizenship across American republics; inferred opposition to long barriers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Bilbao's democratic republic leans toward modest pay but the sources do not say so.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Bilbao's emphasis on individual integrity and free thought suggests members should not be bound by party discipline; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Latinists wanted institutional union of Latin states, and the Latin Union and the monetary union are pooled arrangements; Bilbao's congress would be recognized as the continent's representative.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Imperial strand favored a strong executive, confederal strand did not.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; Bilbao is anticlerical, Catholic Latinists would favor it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Bilbao rejects theocratic pacification and the Latin Union is secular.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Latinists framed conflicts in civilizational terms and expected solidarity with their own Latin government; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Latinists celebrated poetry and literary festivals; Bilbao defended free thought.

recall-officials.rationale: Bilbao favored constant popular self-representation but sources do not discuss recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Napoleonic Latinism built alliances, but anti-US Latin American strands favor autonomy; split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Latinism has no housing doctrine and abolition of renting would be an extreme position it never held.

people-in-arms.rationale: Bilbao proposed a continental army, not citizens' militias.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Mistral's Provencal revivalism had rural romanticism, but the movement took no line.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Bilbao argued Bolivar's divided states should unite federally; inferred to apply to a divided nation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Latinists were literary and scholarly; philologists and writers drove the idea.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Imperial Latinists like Stendhal and Hanotaux ranked Latin peoples as rulers, and the movement presumed Latin civilization's special merit.

death-penalty.rationale: Latin Union states split: most Latin American and European states abolished it, others retain it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; secular republicans favor it, Catholic Latinists oppose it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's freedom-of-thought rationalism and the Latin Union's secular character.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Anachronistic; secular liberals and Catholic traditionalists split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Bilbao proposed universal citizenship across the republics; birthright rules were not discussed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Occitan and Catalan revivalists were central to Latinism, and the Latin Union treated Catalan and Romanian as official languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: French republican secularism and Bilbao's strict church-state separation suggest general laws apply to all; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Bilbao's defence of free thought leans toward it, but Latinism leaned on shared cultural conformity and no source states it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; Bilbao feared economic domination but did not discuss debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Bilbao feared economic as well as political domination, but sources do not say independence requires system change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Bilbao's call for a congress built on popular sovereignty implies constituent assemblies; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Bilbao puts moral ends and freedom above wealth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; the Latin Union's cultural cooperation included development ties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; France's deterrent is Latin but the movement took no line.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Bilbao's popular sovereignty and the republican tradition favor direct popular choice; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary union members relied on state mints, not independent banks; no stated view.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not a Latinist topic and unrelated to its aims.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Bilbao's communal priority suggests property serves social ends; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Marxist debate with no Latinist position.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; no Latinist doctrine bears on it.

collective-defense.rationale: Bilbao argued disunity leaves republics vulnerable and proposed joint action against outside threats.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Bilbao condemned the US annexation of Texas and northern Mexico as conquest.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Bilbao opposed clerical control and called for strict separation; French republican Latinism aligns.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Parliamentary Latin republics hold it, presidential ones do not; Latinism took no line.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Latinists valued unity but also regional autonomy; no stated view.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Federal and regionalist Latinism (Charles-Brun, Mistral) combined larger union with autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Bilbao rejected monarchy, theocracy and hierarchy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's social-justice orientation, which favors progressive burdens.

character-from-environment.rationale: Bilbao blamed Spanish colonial education for servility, which implies environment shapes character; not a stated doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Bilbao opposes despotism and demands republican constitutional government.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Bilbao's congress with equal state representation partly echoes it, but he is republican and never discusses it.

leader-cult.rationale: Bilbao opposed despotism; the Napoleonic strand glorified the emperor, so only mild disagreement.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic family-law question on which Latinists never held a position.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist debate with no Latinist position.

land-redistribution.rationale: Bilbao's call for justice and citizenship might reach land reform, but he proposes no seizure and liberal Latinists oppose it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Latinity was a cultural-linguistic category and the Latin Union required democratic principles; but Romanian and Italian irredentist Latinists made such claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Bilbao defended freedom of thought and rejected theocracy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Foreign to the secular Latin world and Bilbao's liberalism.

common-currency.rationale: The Latin Monetary Union of 1865 standardized coinage among France, Italy, Belgium and Switzerland, and Latinist circles supported it.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Latinism seeks political and cultural unity among peoples sharing Romance languages and descent, from Bilbao's federal congress to Ricard's federation of Latin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Latinists such as Mistral and Charles-Brun backed cultural and regional institutions within states.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Bilbao's universal citizenship and equal rights among peoples favor fighting for rights at home; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bilbao and Latinists saw ideas, morals and race-culture as drivers; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from republican liberalism, which treats concentrated economic power as a danger.

no-bailouts.rationale: The monetary union's weaknesses show tolerance of state financing, but Latinists never took a bailout position.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Bilbao valued a congress with tribunals and rights; inferred opposition to unchecked majority.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement never discussed gender representation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement favored trade ties among Latin states, not closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Bilbao wanted a common international code and a trade pact among republics, which suggests supporting shared standards in trade; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Bilbao puts moral ends above wealth but did not propose replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foreign to the congress-and-treaty method of Latinism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Bilbao cites monarchy and aristocracy as Europe's flaw; republican Latinism agrees.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Latin Union promoted Latin heritage in education; inferred support for civilization-centered teaching.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial Latinists (Napoleon III, Hanotaux) claimed Latin tutelage over others; Bilbao and Charles-Brun rejected conquest; split.

patriotic-education.rationale: Latinist education was pan-national rather than patriotic, while the nation-states they belonged to taught patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; Latin states differ and the movement says nothing.

public-money-creation.rationale: The monetary union standardized state coinage, but Latinists had no theory on who creates money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The movement had no revolutionary economics; the Latin Monetary Union was a reformist commercial arrangement.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Napoleon III and Hanotaux wanted French and Latin influence in Africa and the Americas, and the Latin Union cultivates ties among former colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: Latinists sought commercial integration (monetary union, trade pact); inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist claim foreign to Latinism, which treats Latin peoples as a common civilization rather than as exploiters.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Bilbao supported equal citizenship; inferred opposition.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Bilbao proposed a common code and rights for all citizens; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Bilbao condemned conquest, yet imperial Latinists profited from colonial arrangements; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bilbao and republican Latinists backed popular sovereignty over hereditary monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Bilbao required each state's approval for congress decisions but counted individual votes; not framed as a minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Bilbao opposed despotism and championed revolution against despotic rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Bilbao's popular sovereignty implies elected assemblies as the main lawmaker; the sources never address the monarch question directly.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Bilbao opposed aristocracy but a Catholic cultural strand accepts paternal duties of the rich.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Latinism is an active political and cultural project.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Anachronistic critical theory with no Latinist position.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian claim with no Latinist position.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Bilbao feared US domination, but dependency theory is anachronistic.

native-born-offices.rationale: Bilbao proposed universal citizenship across the republics.

party-own-road.rationale: Bilbao insisted that America create its own path rather than follow others, which favors autonomy from outside direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Bilbao sought self-sufficient American union, but Latinists also sought partnership with Europe.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Bilbao lamented the loss of Texas and northern Mexico but did not demand return.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Bilbao favored incorporation into a universal-citizen republic rather than Indigenous rule.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; the Latin Axis tradition would reject, the Latin Union tradition would accept.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; Latin Union heirs and Latin Axis heirs differ.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Bilbao saw slavery in the US as a central moral issue.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The Latin Union values heritage, but Latinists held no view on contested figures.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Bilbao argued America should create its own moral order rather than copy Europe or the US; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; Latin American strands differ.

filial-duty.rationale: Catholic-cultured Latin societies value filial duty and Latinism celebrated shared tradition; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Bilbao and republican Latinists took offices by election and universal citizenship, not mandarin exams.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Bilbao feared US economic expansion but did not discuss corporate takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic and secular Latinists differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Bilbao's congress required state approval of decisions, which resembles bound delegates, but not stated in this form.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the social, communal orientation of Latinist republicanism.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Bilbao supports republican citizenship and rights without a land-tenure scheme; communal tenure is not documented.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's republican, representative congress model.

single-official-language.rationale: The Latin Union had six official languages including Catalan and Romanian, and Occitan and Catalan revivalists were Latinists.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Bilbao proposed universal citizenship, free movement and colonization among republics, so barring foreigners fits poorly.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic American legal concept with no Latinist position.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Bilbao condemned egoism and the pursuit of wealth for its own sake.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Bilbao rejected conquest and Latinists favored peace; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bilbao insists that union be voluntary, with each state approving congress decisions, so troops sent to stop a member leaving would contradict it; the Napoleonic strand is the exception.

corporate-influence.rationale: Bilbao attacked oligarchic domination of constitutions and wealth-pursuit; inferred sympathy.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Bilbao feared foreign domination, but the sources do not discuss foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Anachronistic; Catholic traditionalists and secular republicans split.

residents-only-property.rationale: Bilbao's trade pact and universal citizenship across republics favor freer property movement.

democratic-peace.rationale: Bilbao argues peace is the unity of liberty and that republics should arbitrate disputes; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Bilbao's republicanism prizes law and constitution, so an adherent would not deny a duty to obey legitimate law.

non-intervention.rationale: Imperial Latinism justified intervention; confederal Latinism and Bilbao opposed foreign intervention; split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities have no place in the sources.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: No Latinist doctrine and inconsistent with both its Catholic and republican cultures.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Bilbao's popular sovereignty and free thought favor transparent government; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Latinism favored trade within the Latin world, but localism is foreign to it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Latinists organized formally through societies, festivals and treaties.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Bilbao proposed a common international code and arbitration tribunal.

religious-nation.rationale: Latin Union membership turns on language and culture, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Napoleonic strand cast France as leader; the confederal strand did not.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regionalists valued autonomy but Latinism did not discuss fiscal redistribution.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: No Latinist source proposes collective ownership of personal goods; republican liberalism protects them.

defeat-communism.rationale: Later Latin Axis heirs lean yes and Latin Union heirs lean coexist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Latin welfare states differ and the movement took no line.

religion-illusion.rationale: Bilbao was anticlerical but still spoke in spiritual and moral terms; Catholic Latinists differ.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; Saint-Simonian Chevalier promoted industrial progress.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Latin Union's multilingual stance and cultural cooperation do not point to linguistic purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: The Latin Monetary Union and Latin Union were treaty-based, and Latinism relied on binding agreements among nations; inferred to treaties generally.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Bilbao admired communal values but not small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inconsistent with Bilbao's inclusive mixed-race vision.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Bilbao sought a third way between European fragmentation and Yankee individualism, but not framed as capitalism versus communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Romanian Latinists invoked Latin ancestry to claim nation status; the movement offers no general principle.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Outside any documented position and contrary to the Latin Union's human-rights commitment.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Latin Union's human-rights commitment and republican tradition point against; not addressed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Bilbao defended freedom of thought and popular sovereignty.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Bilbao was prosecuted for blasphemy and demanded strict Church-State separation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperial Latinists wanted colonial empires, but not in this exploitative form specifically; the confederal strand rejected empire.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Outside the Latin world and unrelated to Latinist doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contradicts Bilbao's rejection of theocratic pacification.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Bilbao favored popular self-representation and universal suffrage; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic theory without any Latinist position.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; Catholic and secular Latin states differ.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Strands ranged from imperial Napoleonic to republican federalist, so no unified stance.

alienated-labor.rationale: Bilbao's critique of division of labor as machine-making is close but not framed through capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; Latin civilization identity is not defined against Islam in the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Bilbao grounds authority in popular sovereignty and rejects theocracy.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's strict Church-State separation and French laicite.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Latin Union's democratic-rights criterion and the continental European Latin states favor social markets; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Bilbao proposed a continental army and defense union.

rich-first.rationale: No Latinist doctrine on development sequencing.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pan-Latinism wanted a Latin bloc against Germanic and Anglo-Saxon powers.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Bilbao rejected hereditary rule as Europe's flaw.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Latin Monetary Union used conventional coinage and banks; inferred disagreement with proposals to reorganize credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anachronistic; Latinists never discussed international lenders.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claim with no Latinist position.

reification.rationale: Marxist-Lukacsian claim with no Latinist position.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Bilbao attacked oligarchic hold on constitutions but did not discuss press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Bilbao opposes despotism and calls for an international code and tribunal; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Bilbao demanded universal suffrage and universal citizenship.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Bilbao's commitment to wide citizen participation.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Contrary to Bilbao's freedom of thought; not addressed directly.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Foreign to Latinism; contrary to the Latin Union's human-rights condition.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Anachronistic; Bilbao favored a representative congress rather than random selection.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Bilbao was anticlerical and Catholic Latinists traditional, so the movement splits.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Bilbao attacked oligarchic constitutions that took powers from citizens.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Bilbao wanted separation of Church and state, not state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; Latinists favored ordered republics.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Bilbao proposed equal state representation in a federal congress, which resembles power sharing among communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Bilbao's emphasis on justice and social duty implies public responsibility, not reliance on charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Bilbao opposed despotism but sources do not say about term limits; Latin American republics themselves differ.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Latinism takes no religious stance; Catholic and secular strands differ.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Modern Latin Union member states have shared marital authority in law; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Bilbao proposed universal citizenship among the republics, not local voting for foreigners.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the Latinist literary and cultural world; not addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Foreign to the republican and cultural Latinists.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Bilbao feared foreign domination but did not discuss bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Bilbao decried the destruction of Indigenous peoples, but state recognition is not addressed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Bilbao prefers justice to power but never theorized income sources.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Bilbao accepted defense of republics against attack.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Latinists traced a shared Roman-Latin descent, but national continuity is not their theme.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic academic claim with no Latinist position.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic academic claim with no Latinist position.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Latin Catholic culture honors martyrs but the movement did not address it.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Bilbao used a spiritual-moral language, but did not cast politics as good versus evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Napoleonic strand cast France as leader of the Latin world, a cultural centre of sorts.

culture-before-state.rationale: Latinism began mostly as literary and cultural networks (festivals, societies) rather than a state project.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Contrary to Bilbao's inclusive republican vision and to universal citizenship.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Latinists favored regional autonomy within states and unions among nations, not merging regions by people.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's popular republican liberty and rejection of despotic centralization.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Marxist debate with no Latinist position.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Regionalist Latinism favored strong local self-government; inferred preference for local public provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Bilbao's congress with equal state representation resembles a federal chamber, but the sources never discuss bicameralism.

municipal-property.rationale: Charles-Brun's regionalism valued local life, but no property doctrine appears.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Ricard's Federation of Latin Peoples and Charles-Brun's Latin confederation envisage a loose federation of free peoples that coordinate and do not rule.

family-wage.rationale: Anachronistic; Catholic social tradition favors it but secular Latinists do not.

person-over-state.rationale: Bilbao insisted on the integrity of the individual against Europe's reduction of persons to functions.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Bilbao describes Latin American values as spiritual and moral, in contrast to Anglo individualism.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Regionalist Latinism (Mistral, Charles-Brun) sought durable autonomy rather than powers revocable by the centre.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Latin race was a linguistic and geographic category in the scholarship, not a biological interest group.

racial-pride.rationale: Latinist festivals celebrated pride in the Latin race as shared heritage, but as culture rather than biology; split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Imperial Latinists accepted expansion; confederal Latinists rejected conquest; split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Latinism holds that Romance-language peoples form one Latin civilization despite state borders, resting on shared language and culture.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not discussed; the republican, confederal strand envisaged citizens of free republics, not religious communities with separate electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Bilbao warned that disunity left the republics prey to US expansion, which suggests a belief in outside threats; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Latin Union states, which mostly fund public higher education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's cultural and monetary aims, not environmental policy.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the confederal movement's long-run vision of a lasting union of peoples.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not discussed; adherents' views on gender followed the diverse cultural views of the era, so no stated position; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: The confederal strand sought arbitration and peaceful union, which implies less arming; inferred from Bilbao's tribunal proposal.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The democratic, republican strand called for a public federal congress; inferred from Bilbao's appeal.

capital-controls.rationale: The Latin Monetary Union aimed at easier flows of coin across member states, so controls on capital are not its model; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not a pan-Latin theme; inferred from the republican, constitutional strand of the confederal mainstream, which favoured orderly state authority.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed; Bilbao's congress would arbitrate disputes, but an individual duty of refusal is not attested and defence is allowed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not a pan-Latin theme; inferred from the democratic republican strand and later Latin Union states with strong labour traditions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Never addressed; the Latin Union states vary widely on in-work credits, so inferred as split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the Latin Monetary Union fixed currency rules but no borrowing limits are attested, so inferred as split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from opposition to US and European domination in Bilbao's appeal and the Latin American strand.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Bilbao's republican federalism sought constitutional federation, not a smashed state; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Not addressed; Latin Union and the confederal idea concern culture and cooperation, not economic experiment, so inferred as split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; nature accounting was never a pan-Latin theme and adherents have no recorded position.

sacred-nation.rationale: Pan-Latinism treats the Latin peoples as an enduring civilization with shared heritage, though the sacred wording is stronger than the sources.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; Latin Union states differ, so inferred as split.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Latin American strand's concern with dependence on outside powers and uneven development.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Bilbao's republican universalism and the Latin world's shared Christian humanist heritage.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the cultural-institutional Latin Union, which promoted shared culture, and the public-media traditions of its states.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Bilbao separated church and state while Latin cultures are largely Catholic; the movement never took a position on a shared truth across religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Never a pan-Latin theme; no source addresses agricultural policy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's proposal to arbitrate disputes rather than go to war and the confederal peaceful strand; nuclear arms were never discussed.

workers-own-party.rationale: Never addressed; the movement was cultural and political-federal rather than class-based.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the democratic, republican strand's rights-based outlook; the sources never mention FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Bilbao's democratic and universal-suffrage commitments; women's land rights are not discussed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the movement's treatment of Romance languages as a linguistic family and the Latin Union's multi-language work; naming disputes were not addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Never addressed by the sources; no basis for a position.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the republican, anti-despotic strand, which would not give hereditary chiefs a legal role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Never addressed; the sources give no basis for ranking environment against liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Never addressed; the confederal strand's liberal rights stance and the imperial strand's order stance would pull in opposite directions.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Never addressed; the Latin Union promoted Romance languages but took no stance on immigrant language requirements.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Never a pan-Latin issue and the Latin states it addressed split on union security; inferred as no clear position.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; voter identification rules vary across the Latin states, so no position is inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the republican, confederal strand's emphasis on free peoples and secular republics, which would not privilege one reading of a religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the democratic, confederal strand of free Latin peoples; the movement never defined democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the modern secularised Latin states the idea later addressed.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the republican, free-peoples outlook of the confederal strand, which would resist cutting communication.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; welfare reform of this kind is not a social-democratic Latin European position.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women's suffrage was not a theme of the 19th-century movement; inferred from the democratic strand and the modern Latin Union states, where it is settled.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; the Latin states it covered are split between Catholic traditionalism and secular feminism, so no position is inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The movement's 'Latin race' was understood as linguistic and cultural rather than biological, which implies race is not a scientific category; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Latin states' modern equality ministries and the Latin Union's cultural-institutional mainstream.

missingStatements.text: The republics of a continent should form a federal union to resist domination by an outside great power.
missingStatements.rationale: Bilbao's 1856 appeal argues that disunity leaves the republics prey to US expansion and calls for a federal congress with joint action.

missingStatements.text: Disputes between neighbouring states should be referred to a common international tribunal before any resort to war.
missingStatements.rationale: Bilbao's proposed congress would arbitrate and no republic could go to war with another without first referring the dispute, except against violent attack.

notes: The imperial strand (Chevalier, Napoleon III, Hanotaux) would answer expansion, tutelage, intervention and leadership items positively; the confederal strand rejects empire. Bilbao was anticlerical, while many Catholic Latinists were not, so religion items are split. No primary source of the French or Italian strands was opened; the scope leans on Bilbao as the primary text.
